items.title: Comparative Assessment of Bio-Oils from Agriculture Biomass Waste and Conventional Fossil Fuels: Evaluating Their Potential as Sustainable Industrial Fuel Alternatives
items.source: ABUAD Journal of Engineering Research and Development (AJERD)
items.summary: The growing demand for sustainable energy and the environmental impacts of fossil fuel dependence have intensified interest in biomass-derived fuels, particularly in developing countries such as Nigeria where agricultural residues remain largely underutilized. This study assessed bio-oils obtained from agricultural biomass in comparison to traditional fossil fuels as a source of industrial energy. Using a vertical silo reactor, bio-oils were produced from mimosa seed pods, banana peels, and cashew nut shells via three thermochemical procedures: torrefaction (200–300 °C), slow pyrolysis (300–500 °C) and fast pyrolysis (>600 °C). items.title: Distillation as a cornerstone for upgrading pyrolysis oils to drop-in fuels: A systematic review and prospects
items.summary: Converting biomass, plastic, and waste tire feedstocks into drop-in fuels is constrained by the poor quality and instability of raw pyrolysis oils. This systematic review synthesises 51 experimental studies published between 2007 and 2025 and evaluates eight distillation-based method categories: simple/atmospheric, fractional, vacuum, molecular, steam, reactive, azeotropic, and catalytic distillation. Distillation improved the biomass oil properties, with mean increases in the higher heating value of 58% and mean water reductions of 76%. items.title: Thermochemical and biochemical conversion technologies for the valorization of coffee-industry residues: a systematic review
items.summary: Introduction The accumulation of agro-industrial residues in the coffee sector poses environmental and logistical challenges. This systematic review analyzes thermochemical and biochemical conversion technologies for the valorization of these streams. Methods Following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines and the PICO strategy, 116 primary studies published between 2020 and 2025 and indexed in Scopus and Web of Science were selected. Results Thermochemical routes, with a focus on slow pyrolysis, and biochemical pathways, such as anaerobic digestion and composting, represent the dominant recovery configurations. items.summary: To address the global warming caused by the elevated atmospheric CO 2 concentration, exploring alternative methods for CO 2 sequestration in plants is crucial. Biogas slurry (BS), which is rich in ammonium nitrogen and alkalinity, can function as a CO 2 carrier. items.summary: Medium chain-methyl ketones are molecules with high energy content and various industrial applications. So far, biotechnological methyl ketone production was performed with glucose as a carbon source in minimal media, which is often not the best choice in terms of achieving a sustainable and cost-efficient bioprocess. We evaluated the application of lignocellulosic hydrolysates as a carbon source derived from agricultural waste streams that do not compete with food production. Notably, we demonstrate that methyl ketone production is feasible from both the cellulosic and hemicellulosic fractions. items.title: Cellulose-based bioplastics for a circular bioeconomy: Properties, applications, market potential, consumer acceptance, and future perspectives
items.summary: Cellulose-based bioplastics have emerged as a promising alternative to conventional petroleum-derived plastics, offering a sustainable and eco-friendly solution to the growing environmental concerns associated with plastic waste. Derived from renewable resources such as wood, cotton, and agricultural residues, cellulose bioplastics exhibit biodegradability, biocompatibility, and low environmental impact. Despite their potential, several challenges impede their widespread adoption. items.title: Conversion and upgrading of microalgal lipids as a potential feedstock for sustainable aviation fuel production
items.summary: Microalgae are widely recognised as a promising feedstock for sustainable aviation fuel (SAF). However, their utilisation in hydroprocessed esters and fatty acids (HEFA) pathways is constrained by the compositional complexity and elevated impurity levels of crude microalgal lipid extracts, which are incompatible with hydrotreating requirements. This study presents a sequential acid-catalysed transesterification and vacuum distillation approach for producing fatty acid methyl esters (FAME) from crude microalgal lipids and evaluating changes in product composition and impurity characteristics relevant to HEFA applications. items.title: Microalgal Bioremediation of Firewood-based Flue Gas for CO2 Fixation
items.summary: Flue gas (FG) contains significant levels of gaseous pollutants that must be effectively managed to prevent air pollution and global warming. The primary components of FG include carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide, sulfur oxides, nitrogen oxides, and trace metals. These pollutants are often removed using physico-chemical methods, which generally incur higher costs. An emerging technique for treating FG involves using microalgae, which have shown promise for efficiently removing and sequestering CO2, SOx, and NOx from FG, while also producing commercially valuable by-products.
